about.title: South Pasadena Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: South Pasadena is a small city, but its main corridors — Fremont Avenue, Fair Oaks Avenue, Huntington Drive, and Monterey Road — carry steady traffic between Pasadena, Los Angeles, and the surrounding San Gabriel Valley. Recent public records show 57 injury collisions and 75 people hurt in a single year, with reports clustering on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., likely tied to commuter and school-pickup traffic. When a crash happens here, the aftermath can be confusing: medical appointments, insurance calls, missed work. LawProactive exists to remove one piece of that burden by connecting you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney who can review your situation and explain your options under California law. You focus on healing; let someone with legal experience handle the insurance conversations and evidence gathering on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but if a government vehicle or roadway defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Acting early protects your right to pursue compensation.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame can lower your payout under pure comparative fault rules. An attorney can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering, But Insurers Still Push Back
items.desc: California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in car accident cases, yet insurance adjusters often try to minimize these claims early. Avoiding a recorded statement and preserving evidence quickly can protect the full value of your claim.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can communicate with the insurer on your behalf instead.

items.question: What if my accident happened near Fair Oaks Avenue or Huntington Drive during heavy Friday traffic?
items.answer: Crashes during peak commute hours on these corridors often involve multiple vehicles and disputed fault, since congestion and quick lane changes are common. Documenting the scene, witness contacts, and any traffic camera footage nearby can strengthen your case. An attorney can help track down this evidence before it disappears.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
